title: A Year Without a Name
thesis: A multi-year drought is ending not with a treaty or a verdict but with a budget line, eroding from emergency into a baseline that no longer makes the front page.
body:
Some crises end with a treaty or a verdict. This one is ending with a budget line, quietly, in a season no one will remember by name [sy_50c2a513f37c, sy_a92b01562ca2].

<then-now>
<then>A year ago the drought was a forecast, and the response was framed as recovery and resilience [sy_50c2a513f37c].</then>
<now>Today it is a fourth failed rains, record displacement, and an aid budget cut at exactly the wrong moment [sy_0c2d35f5f278, sy_a92b01562ca2].</now>
</then-now>

<stat value="4th" label="consecutive failed rainy season across the Horn of Africa">the point at which coping strategies run out [sy_50c2a513f37c]</stat>

<quote display="card">[qt_84f7a6576483]</quote>

The arc here is not escalation toward a climax but erosion toward an absence — the slow conversion of an emergency into a baseline that no longer makes the front page [sy_0c2d35f5f278, sy_a92b01562ca2].
